**Credit name.** Joost de Winter

**Claim.** Nineteen packings beyond n = 324 with sides below the record's standing values on 17 October 2026. From n = 509 to 1568 each packing fits in a square of side below ⌈√n⌉, where the record holds the integer grid. At n = 464 the packing improves Francisco Couzo's certificate of 14 October 2026.

| n | side, rounded up | record on 17 October 2026 |
|---:|---|---|
| 464 | 21.988813022694 | 21.989992144499 (Couzo) |
| 509 | 22.994328036438 | 23 |
| 555 | 23.993653790591 | 24 |
| 603 | 24.995268064197 | 25 |
| 654 | 25.996103908965 | 26 |
| 706 | 26.998712100405 | 27 |
| 760 | 27.995949340329 | 28 |

| 875 | 29.998783733108 | 30 |

| 1568 | 39.999336626159 | 40 |

At each n from 509 to 1568 this packs more squares below the integer side than the record's largest count there (for example 509 against 508 below 23, and 1568 against Kevin Fang's 1564 below 40).

**Certificate.** One exact rational certificate per count, in Evan Daniel's format (line 1 "n side", then "x y t" per square, t = tan(theta/2)), with the decimal poses as JSON:
https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/joostdewinter.github.io/tree/b3152f526f23bc3ae450e51b6e906841233086d1/square-packing-above-324
Pin: commit b3152f526f23bc3ae450e51b6e906841233086d1.

**Checking.**
1. check.py in the folder (Python standard library, exact rational arithmetic): every corner strictly inside the container, every pair with centres closer than sqrt(2) strictly separated along one of the four edge normals. Accepts all 19. Rerun: python3 check.py *.cert (about 1.5 minutes on one core). Least clearances lie between 1e-35 and 2e-11.
2. The printed JSON poses checked again at 80 digits with the true cosine and sine of each printed angle: all 19 valid, same clearances.

**What the checkers share.** One author and the separating-axis method. Route 1 uses the rational half-angle tangents of the certificates; route 2 uses the printed angles directly.

**Not done.** No optimality, rigidity or local-minimum claim. No checker outside the author's has run on these certificates.

**Lineage and credit.** The staircase-rectangle and four-block method of Arslanov, Mustafin and Shangitbayev (Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 28(4), P4.22, 2021): two compressed tilted components and two aligned grids per packing. The n = 464 packing uses a six-square patch transferred from my n = 422 construction.

**AI assistance.** The numerical search and refinement were performed with GPT-6 Astra under my direction. The certificates and checks were produced with Claude (Anthropic).
